title: Commercial terms tiering and revenue trigger playbook
author: Marcus Chen
body:
Summary

This playbook describes how commercial contract terms (pricing tiers, usage modifiers, discounts, bundled services, and commencement triggers) map to billing actions and revenue recognition decisions at Redwood Inference. It is intended for Finance, Legal, Pricing, and Sales Ops. The playbook codifies a decision matrix, an escalation path for non‑standard terms, and representative examples with implementation notes for the billing engine and RevRec journal entries.

Scope

- Applies to all enterprise and dedicated/private deployment contracts (Deals > $50k ARR) and any subscription agreements with non-standard pricing modifiers (e.g., volume tiers, committed burst hours, carryover credits, multi-region add-ons).
- Does NOT replace contract-level legal review; Legal must approve any deviation flagged by this playbook.
- Covers: pricing tiering, effective date vs delivery date, prepaid credits, committed capacity, overage treatment, trial-to-paid cutovers, and marketplace/reseller flows.

Key definitions

1. Effective Date: the date the contract becomes binding. Often the signature date. For RevRec, this is only the start of evaluation; revenue recognition generally aligns to delivery/performance obligations.
2. Commencement Event: the event that begins service delivery for billing and RevRec (examples: activation of VPC link, first inference request, seat provisioning).
3. Billing Trigger: the system-generated event that starts an invoice or consumes pre-paid credits.
4. Committed Capacity: a reserved pool (e.g., Dedicated GPUs) with minimum monthly/annual payments.
5. Modifier: any term that adjusts list price (discount, volume tier, burst add-on, region multiplier).

Decision matrix overview

The table below is the canonical mapping used by Finance and Billing to convert contract terms into system actions and RevRec method. Use this as the first point of reference for pricing or recognition questions.

| Contract Term Type | Billing Trigger | Invoice Timing | RevRec Treatment | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Subscription (flat monthly) | Commencement Event | Monthly in arrears | Recognize evenly over month (monthly performance obligation) | Finance - Billing | Standard SaaS model. |
| Annual prepay (non-refundable) | Effective Date with deferred revenue schedule | Bill at Effective Date | Deferred revenue; recognize monthly/quarterly over contract term | Finance - RevRec | Use amort schedule; tie to contracted term. |
| Committed capacity (reserved GPUs) | Activation of dedicated pool | Monthly/Quarterly per contract | Recognize over committed period; any unused capacity remains prepaid | Finance/Revenue | Track usage separately for churn/true-up. |
| Usage-based (per-token/per-embedding) | First billable request after trial | Monthly in arrears with usage detail | Recognize when usage occurs (consumption) | Billing/Platform | Ensure token counts validated by platform telemetry before invoicing. |
| Overages vs commit | At overage threshold crossing or true‑up date | Invoice on next cycle or immediate true-up invoice | Recognize when overage is billed or service delivered | Finance & Sales Ops | True-ups for committed pools follow contract cadence. |
| One-time setup or professional services | Completion milestone (SOW sign-off) | Bill per milestone | Recognize at milestone completion | GTM / Finance | SOW must specify acceptance criteria. |

Rules and thresholds (operationalized)

- Billing trigger priority: 1) Customer-specified commencement event; 2) Platform activation signal; 3) Effective Date fallback.
- Minimum invoice detail: invoice must include contract id, pricing tier, usage breakdown (tokens, inference-minutes, embeddings), and applied modifiers.
- Dispute threshold: any invoice with a discrepancy > 2% or > $5k should be flagged to FinanceOps for hold and routed to the billing dispute queue.
- Price protection adjustment window: for enterprise multi-year contracts, Pricing adjustments for inflation/cost-pass are allowed only with explicit contractual language; default is no unilateral increase.

Implementation notes for billing engine (technical team tasks)

1. Contract parsing and normalized model: ensure the billing engine stores these normalized fields for every contract: contract_id, effective_date, commencement_event_id, committed_capacity_units, tier_breakpoints, modifiers (type, percent/absolute), billing_cycle, revrec_schedule_id.
2. Event wiring: platform must emit standardized events (activation:event, first_request:event, true_up:date) to the billing queue. These event names should be kept stable; any schema changes require a deprecation notice and 90‑day backwards compatibility.
3. Validation: billing engine should verify token counts against platform telemetry within a 1% tolerance window before invoicing. Exceptions escalate to FinanceOps.
4. Audit trail: every invoice must store a hash of the source contract PDF and a snapshot of the normalized pricing fields used to compute the invoice.

Escalation and approvals (non-standard commercial terms)

1. Sales rep proposes non‑standard modifier (e.g., negative margin commercial term, unusual holdback clause). Sales Ops creates a deviation request in the Contract Deviation tracker and assigns to Pricing.
2. Pricing reviews and produces margin impact and recommended counter-proposals within 3 business days.
3. If margin impact > 15% or legal risk flagged, route to Commercial Review Board (CRB): members include Head of Finance, Lead Counsel, Head of Sales and Head of Product (for technical feasibility). CRB target turnaround: 5 business days.
4. CRB decision recorded in the tracker; if approved, Legal drafts the amendment language and Finance creates corresponding RevRec schedule template.

Representative examples

Example A — Committed Dedicated Pool with Carryover Credits
- Term: 12 months starting Effective Date 2027-03-01
- Committed capacity: 1000 GPU-hours/month, billed monthly at $X/hr; unused hours carry over up to 2 months.
- Billing: bill monthly in arrears based on committed fee; true-up at each quarter if usage > committed + carryover.
- RevRec: Deferred recognition of committed fee over 12 months. Carryover does not change RevRec schedule; usage recognized when consumed.

Example B — Marketplace Reseller Flow (3rd party billing)
- Term: reseller contract; Redwood receives a wholesale payment and transfers service via connector.
- Billing: Redwood invoices reseller per wholesale schedule; reseller invoices the end customer.
- RevRec: Redwood recognizes revenue on delivery to reseller when performance obligation to reseller is satisfied (typically at activation). Ensure reseller agreement includes KPMG-style reseller clauses to determine gross vs net treatment.

Journal entry examples (simplified)

- Annual prepay $120k on 2027-07-01 for 12 months:
  DR Cash $120,000
  CR Deferred revenue $120,000
  Monthly recognition (each month): DR Deferred revenue $10,000; CR Revenue $10,000

- Usage invoice $4,500 for March (tokens verified):
  DR Accounts receivable $4,500
  CR Revenue $4,500

Operational checklists

Onboarding a new enterprise contract (FinanceOps checklist):
1. Receive signed contract; attach PDF to contract record and compute normalized fields.
2. Confirm commencement event and set automated event wiring in platform (owner: Platform Integrations).
3. Create RevRec schedule in accounting system and link schedule id to contract record.
4. Configure rates/tiers in billing engine; create test invoice and route to Sales Ops for validation.
5. Release to Live: confirm first event emissions and invoice generation on next cycle.

Quarterly controls (Finance / RevRec):
- Reconcile deferred revenue schedules to signed contracts and billing records; material variances (>1% or $10k) require a variance memo.
- Review committed capacity utilization across customers; highlight high unused rates (>30%) for Sales to consider commercial remediation.
- Audit 10 random invoices for accuracy of token/usage counts and pricing application.

Change management and documentation

- Any change to billing trigger names or contract normalization schema must be submitted via the Change Request process and include: migration plan, test cases, communication plan, and rollback steps.
- Store canonical pricing modifiers and templates in the Pricing Library (Confluence page) with versioning.

Appendix: sample billing trigger YAML (for platform integrators)

```yaml
contract_id: REDW-2027-0345
effective_date: 2027-03-01
commencement_event: platform.activation.vpc_link
billing_cycle: monthly
pricing:
  base_subscription: { amount: 20000, currency: USD }
  committed_capacity: { units: 1000, unit_type: gpu_hour, price_per_unit: 1.25 }
  modifiers: [ { type: volume_tier, breakpoints: [10000,50000], discounts: [0.03,0.07] } ]
revrec_schedule_id: RS-2027-334
```
